afterSign.text: About the basket: the goose at the bottom was not fruit. It would like an office.
afterSign.subject: geese

clippings.sign: GOOSE GIVEN OFFICE; MAYOR GIVEN GOOSE
clippings.refuse: GOOSE RETURNED TO SENDER, WHO DENIES OWNING A GOOSE

afterRefuse.text: No hard feelings. Please accept this smaller basket. It is one grape.
afterRefuse.subject: ribbons

clippings.sign: MAYOR ACCEPTS GRAPE
clippings.refuse: MAYOR REFUSES GRAPE. GRAPE DEVASTATED

afterSign.text: The pumpkin, now a Freeman of the town, wishes to address the council. It has slides.
afterSign.subject: vegetable-shows

clippings.sign: PUMPKIN'S SPEECH CANCELLED; SLIDES LOST
clippings.refuse: PUMPKIN ADDRESSES EMPTY HALL

afterRefuse.text: The pumpkin has not left its crate since your refusal. It faces the wall.
afterRefuse.subject: vegetable-shows

clippings.sign: MAYOR APOLOGISES TO VEGETABLE
clippings.refuse: PUMPKIN: NO COMMENT

afterSign.text: The ticket museum is full, and so is your drawer. It asks for the shop next door.
afterSign.subject: buses

clippings.sign: MAYOR OPENS MUSEUM ANNEXE; IS ASKED FOR A TICKET
clippings.refuse: TICKET MUSEUM FULL. VISITOR ASKED TO WAIT OUTSIDE

afterRefuse.text: The tickets now fill a shed on the patch. A study asks: is it a museum?
afterRefuse.subject: committees

clippings.sign: STUDY FINDS SHED IS A SHED; ASKS FOR MORE TIME
clippings.refuse: TICKETS STAY IN SHED. SHED SAYS NOTHING

afterSign.text: Rodney wants a portrait of your 7:02. It was late for the sitting.
afterSign.subject: portraits

clippings.sign: MAYOR'S BUS PORTRAIT UNVEILED; BUS MISSES UNVEILING
clippings.refuse: 7:02 STILL NAMED AFTER MAYOR, STILL LATE, STILL WAVING

afterRefuse.text: The 7:02 kept its name, and is on time. Will you wave it off?
afterRefuse.subject: buses

clippings.sign: MAYOR WAVES OFF 7:02; 7:02 LATE FOR FIRST TIME IN WEEKS
clippings.refuse: 7:02 ON TIME AGAIN. NOBODY WAVES

afterSign.text: 38 chimes a day, all for buses. The Guild asks to borrow one.
afterSign.subject: clocks

clippings.sign: CLOCK CHIMES SO OFTEN MAYOR CANNOT HEAR OWN SPEECH
clippings.refuse: CLOCK STAYS WITH BUSES; SHOPS OPEN WITHOUT A CHIME

afterRefuse.text: Denied its bus chimes, the clock sulks. Have a word with it?
afterRefuse.subject: clocks

clippings.sign: MAYOR SEEN TALKING TO CLOCK; CLOCK SAYS NOTHING
clippings.refuse: CLOCK STILL SULKING. SPOTTERS TIME IT

afterSign.text: Rodney proposes a window of you, judging. Labelled WINNER.
afterSign.subject: vanity

clippings.sign: MAYOR'S WINDOW WINS PRIZE; MAYOR WAS THE JUDGE
clippings.refuse: MAYOR DECLINES OWN WINDOW. GLASS RELIEVED

afterRefuse.text: No judge, so every window won. Now a study of the noses on them.
afterRefuse.subject: committees

clippings.sign: STUDY OF WINDOWS FINDS NOSES; NAMES NO NOSES
clippings.refuse: EVERY WINDOW WINS. NONE OF THEM CHEERS

afterSign.text: The 8:15 left with eleven metres of bunting. May it keep them?
afterSign.subject: ceremonies

clippings.sign: BUS LEAVES IN BUNTING; MAYOR WAVES, BUS DOES NOT STOP
clippings.refuse: BUNTING HANDED BACK TO GUILD, FOLDED AND NUMBERED

afterRefuse.text: No bunting, so the Guild hung one ribbon. Will you cut it, Mayor?
afterRefuse.subject: ribbons

clippings.sign: MAYOR CUTS GUILD RIBBON, KEEPS BOTH ENDS
clippings.refuse: RIBBON UNCUT. SHOPPERS STEP OVER IT POLITELY

afterSign.text: Your signpost points to shops 100 % of the time. Buses ask for 50 %.
afterSign.subject: signage

clippings.sign: MAYOR FOLLOWS OWN SIGNPOST, ENDS UP AT BUS STATION
clippings.refuse: SIGNPOST STAYS FAIR: BOTH ARMS STILL POINT AT SHOPS

afterRefuse.text: Each night the signpost turns from the shops. A study will watch.
afterRefuse.subject: signage

clippings.sign: SIGNPOST WATCHED ALL NIGHT, DOES NOTHING; STUDY EXTENDED
clippings.refuse: SIGNPOST TURNS AGAIN. NOBODY WATCHING

afterSign.text: Your turnip came second. Rodney proposes a portrait, cropped to leave out first.
afterSign.subject: portraits

clippings.sign: TURNIP PORTRAIT UNVEILED; LOOKS MORE LIKE MAYOR DAILY
clippings.refuse: SECOND-PLACE TURNIP RETURNS TO PRIVATE LIFE

afterRefuse.text: You would not lend the turnip your name. Till's Teas will pay to lend it theirs.
afterRefuse.subject: vegetable-shows

clippings.sign: TURNIP TAKES TEA SHOP'S NAME; MAYOR ASKS FOR IT BACK
clippings.refuse: TURNIP STAYS NAMELESS. MAYOR'S NAME STILL ON OFFER

afterSign.text: Your scarecrow is photographed more than you. Pose with it, once?
afterSign.subject: vanity

clippings.sign: MAYOR POSES WITH SCARECROW; CAPTION GETS THEM BACKWARDS
clippings.refuse: SCARECROW STANDS ALONE. CROWS STILL UNCONVINCED

afterRefuse.text: No scarecrow? Then a sign: CROWS BY APPOINTMENT ONLY.
afterRefuse.subject: signage

clippings.sign: CROWS MAKE APPOINTMENT; MAYOR'S DIARY FULL
clippings.refuse: CROWS ATTEND WEIGH-IN WITHOUT APPOINTMENT

afterSign.text: The forecourt weigh-in went well. The Society will pay to book it yearly.
afterSign.subject: vegetable-shows

clippings.sign: MAYOR'S HAT WEIGHED BY MISTAKE; COMES THIRD
clippings.refuse: BUSES GET FORECOURT BACK; ONE PUMPKIN LEFT BEHIND

afterRefuse.text: Desmond has logged your refusal under buses. Will you sign it?
afterRefuse.subject: buses

clippings.sign: MAYOR SIGNS BUS NOTEBOOK; IS LOGGED AS LATE
clippings.refuse: NOTEBOOK ENTRY UNSIGNED. SPOTTERS NOTE THAT TOO

afterSign.text: The hats ask to stay on, unless a pumpkin objects in person.
afterSign.subject: hats

clippings.sign: HATS KEEP BANDSTAND; MAYOR TRIES ONE ON, KEEPS IT
clippings.refuse: HATS LEAVE BANDSTAND; PUMPKINS TAKE THE STAGE

afterRefuse.text: The pumpkin show kept its stage. Judge it, Mayor, in a hat?
afterRefuse.subject: vegetable-shows

clippings.sign: MAYOR'S HAT JUDGED BEST IN SHOW, BY MAYOR
clippings.refuse: PUMPKIN SHOW GOES AHEAD. NO HATS, ONE ROSETTE
